title: Geometry-Aware Tabular Diffusion
claim: Relationships between variables can be encoded as explicit pairwise angles and lengths, giving a dense geometric structure that varies by dataset.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right; schematic angle diagram, then two real-data line bundles
description: Three side-by-side plots share a normalized-value y-axis. Panel (a), 'Pairwise Angle Computation', is a toy sketch. Two blue dots, v_i on the left at 0.2 and v_j on the right at 0.75, are joined by a blue line. A dashed horizontal line from v_i and a red arc mark the angle θ_ij. A boxed formula below reads θ_ij = arctan(v_j − v_i). Panels (b) and (c) apply the same idea to real datasets. Each draws many thin lines between 'Col i' and 'Col j' axes, colored by column-type pair: blue for continuous-continuous, orange for continuous-categorical, green for categorical-categorical. Panel (b), Adult, shows a dense tangle of 105 pairs. Panel (c), Default, shows 276 pairs, mostly collapsing into a few steep bundles and a flat green line near −1. Legends give the pair counts. The eye goes first to the colorful tangle in (b).
caption: Geometric Intuition. Inter-column relationships are encoded as pairwise angles θij = arctan(vj −vi) and lengths 2 log(1 + (vj −vi)2), providing explicit relational targets. Diagrams (b) and (c) show sample rows from Adult and Default.
abstract: Tabular synthesis is critical for privacy-preserving sharing and augmentation, yet diffusion models rely on implicit mechanisms to capture inter-column relationships. We introduce Geometry-Aware Tabular Diffusion (GATD), which augments tabular diffusion denoisers with pairwise angles and lengths computed from column value differences and used as inputs and auxiliary targets. Our MLP instantiation achieves state-of-the-art benchmark performance while using 3.5x fewer parameters on average (up to 25x for classification tasks): on ten datasets, it wins 8/10 Shape, 7/10 Trend, and 9/10 downstream utility (F1/RMSE), reducing Shape and Trend error by 27% and 20%. Default loss weights transfer to GNN and Transformer denoisers, improving Shape on 27/30 and Trend on 25/30 architecture-dataset cells. A matched ablation shows supervision (not extra inputs or capacity) drives the gain. This shows explicit relational supervision is a portable inductive bias for tabular diffusion.
